preferred_proof_route: Define W=f+(r:real)/2*norm(x-u)^2. Prove the quadratic derivative directly using HasFDerivAt.norm_sq and const_mul, then add the actual derivative of f.

Identify that derivative with toDual(gradient f x+(r:real)smul(x-u)) using linearity of Riesz toDual and real inner-product evaluation. HasGradientAt.gradient gives actual gradient equality at every x; the same derivative proof yields Differentiable real W.
For strong convexity, use Mathlib strongConvexOn_iff_convex. Expand norm_sub_sq_real so W(x)-r/2*normx² equals f(x) plus the linear functional -r*inner(u,x) plus constant r/2*normu².
The linear functional is convex by LinearMap.convexOn; combine with given convex f using ConvexOn.add and add_const. This works also at r0 and avoids all Hessian assumptions.

For Lipschitz, write gradientW(x)-gradientW(y)=(gradientf(x)-gradientf(y))+r smul(x-y). Triangle inequality, norm_smul and r>=0 give <=(beta+r)*norm(x-y). Use lipschitzWith_iff_norm_sub_le or LipschitzWith.add with a separately proved r-Lipschitz affine map.

recommended_interface.hypotheses: E complete real Hilbert; f Differentiable real and ConvexOn real univ; beta,r:NNReal; LipschitzWith beta (gradient f); centeru arbitrary.
recommended_interface.conclusion: For actual W, Differentiable real W, StrongConvexOn univ (r:real) W, pointwise gradientW=gradientf+r smul(x-u), LipschitzWith(beta+r)(gradientW).
recommended_interface.endpoint: Allow r0 and beta0; these are mathematically valid. The source positive delta specialization comes later. Do not call W strictly convex for r0 or claim unique minimizer without attainment and r>0.
recommended_interface.C1: Differentiable f plus Lipschitz actual gradient supplies C1-type regularity in the intended real Hilbert setting; an explicit ContDiff1 output is unnecessary unless a consumer needs it. Differentiable W output is useful and free from the proof.
recommended_interface.substance: This removes load-bearing C2/Hessian requirements from the existing shift interface and supplies the actual gradient needed for first-order oracle simulation. One bundle is appropriate; no standalone wrapper for each conjunct.
